pack.name: NIS2 Directive — EU baseline
coverage: selected cybersecurity risk-management measures under Article 21
known_gaps: NIS2 is a directive; national law, competent-authority guidance and sector-specific Union acts must be overlaid.
This pack does not decide entity scope from sector, size and establishment facts.
Detailed incident timelines and national notification channels require jurisdiction profiles.
Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 and sector-specific requirements are not encoded.
pack.notice: Use this pack only as an EU baseline together with a reviewed national overlay.

fact_catalog.question: Is the entity essential, important, out of scope or unresolved under applicable national law?
Does the management body approve and oversee cybersecurity risk measures?
Do management-body members receive required cybersecurity training?
Are appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures implemented?
Does the programme address supply-chain security?
Is there an operational process for significant-incident reporting?

anchors.locator: Articles 2 and 3; Annexes I and II
anchors.summary: Scope and distinction between essential and important entities, subject to the Directive and national transposition.
Management bodies approve and oversee measures, may face liability under national law, and must receive training.
Appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures, including ten listed areas.
Notification duties for significant incidents, with staged reporting.

finding.title: The entity is recorded as essential or important
finding.summary: The NIS2 governance, risk-management and reporting baseline applies, subject to national law and sector-specific rules.

obligations.title: Pin the relevant national-transposition and sector profile.

finding.title: Management-body approval and oversight are not evidenced
finding.summary: An in-scope entity lacks evidence that its management body approves and oversees Article 21 measures.

obligations.title: Establish approval, oversight and accountable reporting to the management body.

finding.title: Management-body cybersecurity training is not evidenced
finding.summary: The in-scope entity has not evidenced the training required for management-body members.

obligations.title: Provide and evidence proportionate management-body training.

finding.title: Appropriate and proportionate risk measures are not evidenced
finding.summary: The in-scope entity lacks evidence of an Article 21 cybersecurity risk-management programme.

obligations.title: Map and implement the Article 21(2) areas using an all-hazards, proportionate approach.

finding.title: Supply-chain security is not evidenced
finding.summary: Security aspects of relationships with direct suppliers and service providers are not established.

obligations.title: Assess supplier vulnerabilities and the quality and resilience of supplier security practices.

finding.title: A significant-incident reporting process is not evidenced
finding.summary: The in-scope entity lacks an operational process aligned to applicable staged notification duties.

obligations.title: Implement the applicable national early-warning, notification and final-report workflow.
